# zoxide 0.9.9 — CLI parsing & help/error text spec (byte-exact)

Binary: `/workspace/executable`. Parser is **clap v4** with `wrap_help` **disabled** and `color` **disabled** (proven below). All experiments used a fresh `_ZO_DATA_DIR`.

---

## 0. Global invariants

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Help/version stream | **stdout**, exit **0** |
| All parse errors | **stderr**, exit **2** |
| Runtime (post-parse) errors | **stderr**, exit **1** |
| Error trailer (always, exactly) | `For more information, try '--help'.` + `\n` |
| Colorization | **never** — no ANSI bytes, even on a pty, with any of `TERM=xterm-256color`, `CLICOLOR=1`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`, `FORCE_COLOR=1`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `NO_COLOR=1` |
| Terminal-width sensitivity | **none** — output byte-identical at `COLUMNS=40`, pty `stty cols 40`, pty `stty cols 200`, and pipe |
| Locale sensitivity | **none** — identical under `LC_ALL/LANG` = `C`, `POSIX`, `C.UTF-8`, `de_DE.UTF-8`, `ja_JP.UTF-8` |
| Long-flag prefix matching (`infer_long_args`) | **OFF** (`query --lis` errors) |
| Subcommand prefix matching (`infer_subcommands`) | **OFF** (`ad`, `quer`, `ini` all error) |
| `help` as a subcommand | **does not exist** |
| `@file` argfiles | not supported (`@foo` → unrecognized subcommand) |
| Every output ends with exactly one `\n`; no CR anywhere | verified with `od` |

### Program-name (`bin_name`) derivation
`bin_name` = `Path::file_name(argv[0])`, falling back to the literal `zoxide` when `file_name()` yields nothing.

```
argv[0]                  Usage shows
'zoxide'              -> zoxide
'/a/b/c/myprog'       -> myprog
'myprog.exe'          -> myprog.exe
'trailing/'           -> trailing
'sub/dir/name'        -> name
''                    -> zoxide      (fallback)
'.'                   -> zoxide      (fallback)
'..'                  -> zoxide      (fallback)
'/'                   -> zoxide      (fallback)
'  spaced  '          -> "  spaced  "  (kept verbatim, incl. spaces)
'日本語'               -> 日本語
'a\tb'                -> a\tb
```
Command used: `python3 -c "subprocess.run(['/a/b/c/myprog','--help'], executable='/workspace/executable')"`, and `ln -s /workspace/executable /tmp/probe/x/frobnicate`.

### Version/display-name derivation — **hardcoded, NOT argv[0]**
`/tmp/probe/x/frobnicate --help` still prints `zoxide 0.9.9` on line 1; `frobnicate add --help` prints `zoxide-add 0.9.9`. The display name is `zoxide` joined with the subcommand path by `-`.

```
[]                 zoxide 0.9.9
[add]              zoxide-add 0.9.9
[edit]             zoxide-edit 0.9.9
[import]           zoxide-import 0.9.9
[init]             zoxide-init 0.9.9
[query]            zoxide-query 0.9.9
[remove]           zoxide-remove 0.9.9
[edit increment]   zoxide-edit-increment 0.9.9
[edit decrement]   zoxide-edit-decrement 0.9.9
[edit delete]      zoxide-edit-delete 0.9.9
[edit reload]      zoxide-edit-reload 0.9.9
```
`-V` and `--version` are byte-identical everywhere. **Every** subcommand, including the four hidden `edit` subcommands, supports both `-V` and `--version`.

### `-h` vs `--help`
**Byte-identical** for all 11 commands (`diff` clean for `""`, `add`, `edit`, `import`, `init`, `query`, `remove`, `edit increment|decrement|delete|reload`).

---

* **clap default template** (the four hidden `edit` subcommands): no version/author/URL/about/env sections, and `Usage: ` is inline on one line.

All blocks below are `cat -A` output; `$` = end of line. **`<SP>`** is used only in the annotations — the literal bytes are shown by the `$` position.

## 2. `-h`/`--help`, `-V`, `help`, `--help` after `--`

* `-h` ≡ `--help` byte-for-byte for all 11 commands.
* `-V` ≡ `--version` for all 11 commands. Every subcommand (including hidden ones) has `-V/--version`.
* **`help` is not a subcommand**: `executable help` and `executable help add` both produce `error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'` (exit 2). Note there is **no** "tip" for `help` — nothing similar enough.
* `executable add help` → `help` is consumed as a path → `zoxide: not a directory: $PWD/help`, exit 1.
* **No `--help` after `--`.** `executable -- --help` → `error: unrecognized subcommand '--help'`. `executable query -- --help` → `--help` becomes a keyword → `zoxide: no match found`, exit 1.

**Help/version precedence** (all exit 0):
| argv | result |
|---|---|
| `--help add` | top-level help |
| `query --help --bogus` | query help (help wins, later junk ignored) |
| `query --bogus --help` | **error** `unexpected argument '--bogus'` (exit 2) — earlier error wins |
| `query foo --help` | query help |
| `add --help extra` | add help |
| `-V query` | `zoxide 0.9.9` |
| `query --help -V` | query **help** (first wins) |
| `query -V --help` | `zoxide-query 0.9.9` (first wins) |
| `-hl`, `query -hl`, `query -lh` | help (help short-circuits inside a cluster, in either position) |

---

## 3. Stream / exit-code matrix

| Case | Stream | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--help` / `-h` (any level) | stdout | 0 |
| `--version` / `-V` (any level) | stdout | 0 |
| **no args** | **stderr** — full top-level long help verbatim (byte-identical to `--help` on stdout, `diff` clean) | **2** |
| bare `--` only | **stderr** — same full long help | **2** |
| unknown subcommand | stderr | 2 |
| missing required arg | stderr | 2 |
| bad enum value | stderr | 2 |
| unknown flag | stderr | 2 |
| flag given bad value (`--score x`) | stderr | 2 |
| missing value for flag (`--cmd`) | stderr | 2 |
| unexpected value on a boolean flag (`--all=1`) | stderr | 2 |
| conflicting flags (`-l -i`) | stderr | 2 |
| repeated non-multiple flag (`-l -l`) | stderr | 2 |
| invalid UTF-8 in a `String` arg | stderr | 2 |
| empty value for a `PathBuf` positional | stderr | 2 |
| any runtime failure (`no match found`, `not a directory`, `could not find fzf`, import IO) | stderr | 1 |

`--help` to `/dev/full` still exits **0** with empty stderr. `executable --help \| head -1` leaves exit status **0** (no EPIPE-driven failure observed).

Subcommand-with-no-args behaviour: `add` → error 2; `import` → error 2; `init` → error 2; `edit` → runs (exit 1 without fzf); `query` → runs (exit 1 `no match found` on empty DB); `remove` → **exit 0, no output**; `edit increment|decrement|delete` → error 2 (missing `<PATH>`); `edit reload` → runs.

---

## 4. Exact error text, per failure mode

Structural rule: `error: <msg>\n` `\n` [`  tip: <t>\n` `\n`] [`Usage: <one-line usage>\n` `\n`] `For more information, try '--help'.\n`.
The `Usage:` line in **errors is always the single-line inline form** (`Usage: executable query …`) even for commands whose *help* uses the multi-line `Usage:\n  …` template.

Errors that **omit** the `Usage:` block entirely: `invalid value …` (enum + parse failures), `a value is required for '…' but none was supplied`.

### 4.1 Unrecognized subcommand
```
error: unrecognized subcommand 'foo'$
$
Usage: executable <COMMAND>$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
With a near-miss (`ad`, `quer`, `ini`) an extra tip block appears:
```
error: unrecognized subcommand 'ad'$
$
  tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'add'$
$
Usage: executable <COMMAND>$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
`quer` → `'query'`; `ini` → `'init'`. Case-sensitive: `QUERY` gets **no** tip. `''` → `error: unrecognized subcommand ''`. `-` → `error: unrecognized subcommand '-'`.

**Plural tip form exists for subcommands** (`executable e`):
```
error: unrecognized subcommand 'e'$
$
  tip: some similar subcommands exist: 'remove', 'edit'$
$
Usage: executable <COMMAND>$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
`edit d`:
```
error: unrecognized subcommand 'd'$
$
  tip: some similar subcommands exist: 'decrement', 'delete'$
$
Usage: executable edit$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
Note the list is **not** alphabetical — it is confidence-ordered (`'remove', 'edit'` for `e`; `'import', 'init'` for `i`; `'decrement', 'increment', 'reload'` for `r`).

### 4.2 Unknown flag
No similar flag, but the command has a positional → "pass as value" tip:
```
error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found$
$
  tip: to pass '--bogus' as a value, use '-- --bogus'$
$
Usage: executable query [OPTIONS] [KEYWORDS]...$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
Same shape for `query -z`, `query -1`, `remove --bogus`.
No similar flag **and no positional** (`edit`, `edit reload`) → **no tip**:
```
error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found$
$
Usage: executable edit$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```

### 4.3 Near-miss flag suggestions
Only the **singular** form is ever produced for arguments (exhaustively verified: all 1–3-char `--xxx` over `[a-z]` for every command, plus all 65 536 4-char combos over `cmdnohkelpvrsia-` on `init` → **zero** occurrences of "some similar arguments exist").

The `Usage:` line in these errors **incorporates the suggested flag**:
```
error: unexpected argument '--lis' found$
$
  tip: a similar argument exists: '--list'$
$
Usage: executable query --list [KEYWORDS]...$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
```
error: unexpected argument '--intractive' found$
$
  tip: a similar argument exists: '--interactive'$
$
Usage: executable query --interactive [KEYWORDS]...$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
Other confirmed pairs (`tip` → `Usage`):
| input | tip | Usage line |
|---|---|---|
| `query --al` | `'--all'` | `executable query --all [KEYWORDS]...` |
| `query --exclud` | `'--exclude'` | `executable query --exclude <path> [KEYWORDS]...` |
| `query --base` / `--basedir` | `'--base-dir'` | `executable query --base-dir <path> [KEYWORDS]...` |
| `add --scor` / `--sore` | `'--score'` | `executable add --score <SCORE> <PATHS>...` |
| `import --form` | `'--from'` | `executable import --from <FROM> <PATH>` |
| `import --merg` | `'--merge'` | `executable import --from <FROM> --merge <PATH>` |
| `init bash --ho` / `--hoo` | `'--hook'` | `executable init --hook <HOOK> <SHELL>` |
| `init bash --z-cmd z` | `'--no-cmd'` | `executable init --no-cmd <SHELL>` |
| `init bash --no-alias` | `'--no-aliases'` | `executable init --no-cmd <SHELL>` ← tip names the **alias**, Usage names the **canonical** flag |
| `--verbose` (top) | `'--version'` | `executable --version <COMMAND>` |
| `--hel` (top) | `'--help'` | `executable --help <COMMAND>` |
| `--vers` (top) | `'--version'` | `executable --version <COMMAND>` |
| `---help` (top) | `'--help'` | `executable --help <COMMAND>` |

Single letters do trigger suggestions: `query --a`→`'--all'`, `query --i`→`'--list'`, `query --s`→`'--score'`, `query --e`→`'--help'`, `query --b`→`'--base-dir'`, `query --c`→`'--score'`, `query --h`→`'--help'`; `query --m`, `query --f`, `query --sl`, `query --cd` get the "pass as a value" tip instead.

### 4.5 Bad enum value
```
error: invalid value 'badshell' for '<SHELL>'$
  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, nushell, posix, powershell, tcsh, xonsh, zsh]$
$
  tip: a similar value exists: 'bash'$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
The possible-values line is indented **2 spaces** and is on the line immediately after the `error:` line (no blank line between). **No `Usage:` block.**

Without a close match (`init BASH`):
```
error: invalid value 'BASH' for '<SHELL>'$
  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, nushell, posix, powershell, tcsh, xonsh, zsh]$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
Enums are **case-sensitive**: `Bash` → invalid (+ tip `'bash'`), `NONE` → invalid, `Z` → invalid.

`init bash --hook bogus`:
```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--hook <HOOK>'$
  [possible values: none, prompt, pwd]$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
`import --from=bogus f`:
```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--from <FROM>'$
  [possible values: autojump, z]$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
`import --from autojum f` adds `  tip: a similar value exists: 'autojump'`.

Value-suggestion tip is **singular only** — exhaustive 1–3-char sweep over `[a-z]` for `<SHELL>` produced zero "some similar values exist". Suggestions observed: `bash, elvish, fish, nushell, posix, powershell, tcsh, xonsh, zsh` — **never `ksh`** (see §6).

### 4.6 Missing value for a flag (no `Usage:` block)
```
error: a value is required for '--cmd <CMD>' but none was supplied$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
Same for `--score <SCORE>`, `--exclude <path>`, `--base-dir <path>`.
`query --exclude -l` produces the *same* message (a following `-l` is **not** consumed as a value).
`add -s -- /tmp` also produces the same message (`--` does not supply the value).
For an enum option the possible-values line is appended (`import --from= x`):
```
error: a value is required for '--from <FROM>' but none was supplied$
  [possible values: autojump, z]$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```
Empty `PathBuf` positional (`add ""`, `import --from z ""`) reuses this kind — verified byte-exact by `od`:
```
error: a value is required for '<PATHS>...' but none was supplied$
$
For more information, try '--help'.$
```

## 5. Value-attachment syntax

| Form | Long options | Short options |
|---|---|---|
| `--flag value` / `-s value` | ✅ `--score 1`, `--cmd q`, `--hook none`, `--from z`, `--exclude /tmp`, `--base-dir /tmp` | ✅ `-s 1` |
| `--flag=value` / `-s=value` | ✅ `--score=1`, `--cmd=q`, `--hook=none`, `--from=bogus`, `--exclude=/tmp`, `--base-dir=/tmp` | ✅ `-s=1` and `-s=-1` |
| `-sVALUE` (attached) | n/a | ✅ `-s1` |
| `--flag=` (empty) | accepted for `String` options (`--cmd=`, `--exclude=`); rejected for typed (`--score=` → float parse error) and for enums (`--from=` → "a value is required", exit 2) | — |

Boolean flags reject `=value` (`--all=1`, `--help=x` → §4.8). `-a=1` is parsed as the cluster `-a`, `-=` → `error: unexpected argument '-=' found` with tip `to pass '-=' as a value, use '-- -='`.

**Negative numbers are not values:** `add -s -1 /tmp` → `error: unexpected argument '-1' found` + `tip: to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'`. Use `-s=-1` or `--score=-1`. There is no `allow_negative_numbers`; `query -1` is likewise rejected.

**Combined short flags work:** `query -ls`, `query -lsa`, `query -hl`, `query -lh`, `query -il` all cluster correctly.

**`--` semantics:** ends option parsing for the current (sub)command. `query -- -1`, `query -- --`, `query -- -l`, `query a -- b`, `query -- a -l` all treat the tail as keywords (exit 1 `no match found` on an empty DB). `add -- --score 1` treats `--score` and `1` as paths. `remove -- --bogus` → `zoxide: path not found in database: --bogus`. `init -- bash` and `init bash --` both work (exit 0). A bare `--` as the only argv → full help on stderr, exit 2. An argument that is exactly `--` *after* another `--` is a literal keyword.

**Positional/flag interleaving is allowed:** `query --list foo --score` → exit 0.
**Extra positionals are rejected:** `init bash zsh` → `error: unexpected argument 'zsh' found`, `Usage: executable init [OPTIONS] <SHELL>`; `init bash extra1 extra2` → reports `'extra1'`; `import --from z a b` → reports `'b'`, `Usage: executable import [OPTIONS] --from <FROM> <PATH>`; `edit increment a b` → reports `'b'`, `Usage: executable edit increment <PATH>`; `edit reload extra` → reports `'extra'`, `Usage: executable edit reload`.

# zoxide 0.9.9 — rank / score / aging arithmetic: reverse-engineered spec

All results below were obtained by running `/workspace/executable` only, with hand-crafted `db.zo` files (python3 `struct`) and a fake `fzf` on `PATH`. Every claim was executed and observed. Notation: `<SP>` = 0x20, `<TAB>` = 0x09, `<NUL>` = 0x00, `<LF>` = 0x0A.

---

## 0. Database file format (needed to state everything else)

`$_ZO_DATA_DIR/db.zo`, little-endian, no padding, no trailing bytes:

```
u32   version          (must be exactly 3)
u64   entry_count
repeat entry_count times:
    u64   path_len
    u8[path_len]  path (raw bytes, NOT canonicalized on read)
    f64   rank
    u64   last_accessed   (Unix epoch SECONDS)
```

Observed reference dump after a single `add /tmp`:

```
03 00 00 00 | 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 | 04 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 |
2f 74 6d 70 | 00 00 00 00 00 00 f0 3f | 67 56 79 6a 00 00 00 00
version=3     count=1                   len=4  "/tmp"  rank=1.0   ts=1786467943-ish
```

Version errors (exit 1, stderr):
* `zoxide: unsupported version (got 0, supports 3)<LF>` — same text for 1, 2, 4, 255.
* Truncated file: `zoxide: could not deserialize database<LF><LF>Caused by:<LF>    io error: unexpected end of file<LF>`
* Zero-byte file: `zoxide: could not deserialize database: corrupted data<LF>`
  (A **missing** file is fine — treated as an empty database.)

Only `db.zo` is created in `_ZO_DATA_DIR`; no leftover temp files after a successful run.

## 1. score(rank, age) — EXACT

```
now  = wall-clock Unix epoch seconds (u64, from SystemTime)
age  = now.saturating_sub(last_accessed)      // BOTH are u64; no signed arithmetic

age <      3_600  ->  score = rank * 4.0
age <     86_400  ->  score = rank * 2.0
age <    604_800  ->  score = rank / 2.0
otherwise         ->  score = rank / 4.0
```

Boundaries verified byte-exactly in a single clock-second (`T0=$(date +%s)` before, `date +%s` after, retried until stable), rank = 3.0:

| age (s) | printed |
|---|---|
| 3598 | `  12.0` |
| 3599 | `  12.0` |
| **3600** | `   6.0` |
| 3601 | `   6.0` |
| 86398 | `   6.0` |
| 86399 | `   6.0` |
| **86400** | `   1.5` |
| 86401 | `   1.5` |
| 604798 | `   1.5` |
| 604799 | `   1.5` |
| **604800** | `   0.8` (= 0.75) |
| 604801 | `   0.8` |

So the thresholds are **`< 3600`, `< 86400`, `< 604800`** (i.e. HOUR = 3600, DAY = 86400, WEEK = 604800), strict `<`.

**Negative / future timestamps.** The timestamp field is **unsigned 64-bit**, and the subtraction **saturates at 0**:

* `last_accessed = now + 1` → `   4.0` (age 0)
* `last_accessed = now + 100000` → `   4.0`
* `last_accessed = 0x8000000000000000` (2^63) → `   4.0`
* `last_accessed = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` (u64::MAX) → `   4.0`
* `last_accessed = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFC18` (i64 `-1000`) → `   4.0`  ← proves u64, not i64 (an i64 read would give `now+1000` age → `/4`)
* `last_accessed = 0` → age = now (≈1.79e9 > WEEK) → `rank/4`; rank 1.0 → `   0.2`
* `last_accessed = 1` → same, `   0.2`

There is **no separate "future" branch** — future timestamps simply become age 0 and get the ×4 multiplier.

`rank/2` and `rank/4` are indistinguishable from `rank*0.5` / `rank*0.25` in IEEE-754, so no experiment can separate them.

## 2. `query --list --score` output format — EXACT

```
line = format!("{score:>6.1}") + "<SP>" + path + "<LF>"

where
```

### 2c. Ordering (matters for reproducing output)

`query` **sorts the in-memory list ascending by raw (unclamped) score using `f64::total_cmp`, stably, and then prints it in reverse**, i.e. descending. Proof:
* `-NaN` sorts first (printed last), then `-inf`, `1.0`, `+inf`, `+NaN` last (printed first). Exactly `total_cmp` order.
* Ties keep insertion order in the ascending list, hence appear **reverse-insertion-order** in the printed (descending) output. E.g. 5 entries all scoring 4.0 inserted a,b,k,l,n printed `n,l,k,b,a`.
* Sort key is the **score**, not the rank: `/p rank=100 age=0` (400.0) sorts above `/q rank=1000 age=1e6` (250.0).

**`query` PERSISTS this sort to disk**, even when it exits 1 with "no match found":
```
before: /zz(9.0) /aa(1.0)   →  after `query nomatchxyz` (exit 1):  /aa(1.0) /zz(9.0)
```
Ranks and timestamps are **not** modified by `query` — only the entry order.

`edit reload` does **not** sort; it emits the entries in **reverse database order**.

## 3. `add` — rank arithmetic

Model (matches every observation):

```
by = --score value, default 1.0
if entry exists (FIRST match by exact stored string):
    rank = f64::max(rank + by, 0.0)
else:
    push new entry with rank = f64::max(by, 0.0)
in both cases: last_accessed = now
then: age_database()   // see §5
```

`f64::max` semantics matter: `f64::max(NaN, x) == x`, which is why NaN inputs collapse to `0.0`.

* **New entry, no `--score`: rank = 1.0.**
* **Existing entry, no `--score`: rank += 1.0.** Four consecutive `add /tmp` → 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0.
* `add` **requires the path to exist and be a directory**; otherwise exit **1**, stderr `zoxide: not a directory: /nope<LF>` and the db is untouched. Relative paths are resolved against cwd before this check.
* `add A A A` in one invocation → rank 3.0 (each path processed independently).
* `add --score N A B` applies N to **every** path.
* `add` does **not** reorder the database.
* Duplicate stored paths: only the **first** matching entry is incremented.

## 4. `edit increment` / `edit decrement`

`edit` has **hidden subcommands** (not listed in `edit --help`): `increment <PATH>`, `decrement <PATH>`, `delete <PATH>`, `reload`. Each takes exactly one PATH (`increment /a /b` → `error: unexpected argument '/b' found`). Unknown subcommand → exit 2, `error: unrecognized subcommand 'bogus'`.

```
edit increment P :  rank = f64::max(rank + 1.0, 0.0)
edit decrement P :  rank = f64::max(rank - 1.0, 0.0)
```

Key properties, all verified:

* **The timestamp is NOT touched.** db entry `("/e", 5.0, 1234567890)` → after `edit increment /e` it is `("/e", 6.0, 1234567890)`; after `edit decrement /e` back to `("/e", 5.0, 1234567890)`.
* **The path is NOT validated or canonicalized.** `edit increment /no/such/dir` succeeds (exit 0) and stores the literal string; `edit increment relpath` stores the literal string `relpath` (no cwd resolution).
* **On a missing entry it creates one** with `rank = max(±1.0, 0.0)` and `last_accessed = now`: `increment` → rank `1.0`, `decrement` → rank **`0.0`**.
* **Reaching rank 0 does NOT delete the entry.** There is no deletion threshold in `decrement` at all — rank simply saturates at `0.0` and the row stays. Only `edit delete` (or `remove`, or aging) removes rows.
* **Aging is never run.** A db whose ranks sum to 20001 was left untouched by `edit increment` (`sum` stayed 20001), and `_ZO_MAXAGE=abc` produces no error.
* Both print the edited entry, then exit 0, in the fzf format: `{score:>6.1}<TAB>path<NUL>` — using the **new rank** but the **old timestamp**. Example: rank 0.0, ts = now−100000 (DAY..WEEK band → `/2`); after `increment` rank = 1.0 → printed `<SP><SP><SP>0.5<TAB>/e<NUL>`.

## 5. Aging (`_ZO_MAXAGE`) — EXACT algorithm

### When it runs
**Only in `add`, exactly once, after all `<PATHS>` have been applied.** Verified NOT to run in: `query` (any flags), `remove`, `edit increment`, `edit decrement`, `edit delete`, `edit reload`, `import --from z`, `import --from z --merge`, `import --from autojump`. Corroboration: `_ZO_MAXAGE=abc` only produces an error under `add`; all other subcommands succeed.

"Once at end" proof (`_ZO_MAXAGE=10`, db `/a` rank 20.0, `add R1 R2`): result `/a = 8.181818181818182` = `20·(0.9·10/22)`. Per-path aging would have produced `20·(0.9·10/21) = 8.571428571428571` plus a surviving `R2=1.0`.

### The algorithm

```
max_age : f64  = _ZO_MAXAGE parsed as u32 (default 10000), then widened to f64
sum     : f64  = fold over dirs IN DATABASE ORDER, left-to-right:  s = 0.0; for d: s += d.rank

if sum > max_age {                        // STRICT greater-than
    factor = 0.9 * max_age / sum          // evaluated as ((0.9 * max_age) / sum)
    for idx in (0 .. len).rev() {         // reverse index order
        dirs[idx].rank *= factor
        if dirs[idx].rank < 1.0 {         // STRICT less-than; NaN fails => KEPT
            dirs.swap_remove(idx)         // last element is moved into slot idx
        }
    }
}
```

Every clause above was pinned down individually:

**Trigger is strict `>`.** `_ZO_MAXAGE` unset (=10000), db `/filler=9999.0` + `add` of a new dir (rank 1.0) → sum exactly `10000.0` → **no aging** (`/filler=9999.0`, new entry `=1.0` both kept). Changing filler to `nextafter(9999.0, +inf)` → sum `10000.000000000002` → aging fired (`/filler=8999.1`, new entry deleted). Same result with `_ZO_MAXAGE=6` and sum exactly 6.

**Default max_age = 10000** (from the two experiments above).

**Sum is a plain left-to-right f64 fold in database order.** db `[1e16, 1.0, 1.0]` + added `1.0`: left-to-right gives exactly `1e16`, so `/big` became exactly `9000.0`. Reverse order or `fsum` would give `1.0000000000000004e16` → `8999.999999999996`. Observed: `9000.0`.

**Factor association is `(0.9 * max_age) / sum`, not `0.9 * (max_age / sum)`** (differs by 1 ULP). Distinguishing runs, single surviving entry `/big` with rank R, plus one added dir at 1.0 so `sum = R+1`:

| `_ZO_MAXAGE` | R | observed `/big` | `(0.9·M)/S·R` | `0.9·(M/S)·R` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 4 | `1.44` | `1.44` ✔ | `1.4400000000000002` ✘ |
| 3 | 6 | `2.3142857142857145` | `2.3142857142857145` ✔ | `2.314285714285714` ✘ |
| 4 | 4 | `2.88` | `2.88` ✔ | `2.8800000000000003` ✘ |
| 6 | 6 | `4.628571428571429` | `4.628571428571429` ✔ | `4.628571428571428` ✘ |

**Delete cutoff is `scaled_rank < 1.0` (strict), i.e. exactly 1.0 survives.** Constructed so `factor == 0.5` exactly (`sum = 18000`, max_age = 10000 → `9000/18000`):
db `[/filler=17993.0, /A=2.0, /B=nextafter(2.0,0)=1.9999999999999998, /C=nextafter(2.0,4)=2.0000000000000004, /real=0.0]`, then `add /real` (→ 1.0). Result:
```
/filler = 8996.5
/A      = 1.0                      (exactly 1.0, KEPT)
/C      = 1.0000000000000002       (KEPT)
/B      deleted (0.9999999999999999)
/real   deleted (0.5)
```

**NaN ranks survive** (because `NaN < 1.0` is false — a `retain(rank >= 1.0)` would have deleted them). db `[/inf = +inf, /x = 5.0]` + `add /r1`: sum = inf > 10000, factor = `0.9*10000/inf = 0.0`; `/inf` → `inf*0 = NaN` **kept**, `/x` → `0.0` deleted, `/r1` → `0.0` deleted. Final db: one entry, `/inf` with rank `nan`.

**Negative and zero ranks are deleted** when aging fires (`-x*factor < 1.0`), and they **contribute negatively to the sum**: db `[/big=20000, /neg=-5, /zero=0]` + `add` → sum `19996`, factor `0.45009001800360073`, result: only `/big = 9001.800360072015`. Conversely a db summing to a negative number never triggers aging (`[-100, -50]` + `add` → nothing scaled, all three rows kept).

**Deletion uses reverse-index `swap_remove`, which REORDERS the database.** Two independent confirmations (`_ZO_MAXAGE` unset):

Test A — db order `e0=5000, e1=1, e2=4000, e3=1, e4=3000, e5=2000, real=0`; `add real`; sum = 14002, factor = `0.6427194172677283`; e1, e3, real fall below 1.0.
Resulting file order: **`e0, e4, e2, e5`** (a `retain` would give `e0, e2, e4, e5`).

Test B — db order `e0=1, e1=5000, e2=1, e3=4000, e4=3000, real=0`; sum = 12002; e0, e2, real deleted.
Resulting file order: **`e3, e1, e4`** (a `retain` would give `e1, e3, e4`).

Each entry is scaled exactly once (the element moved by `swap_remove` always came from an already-processed higher index).

**Consequence — a hard cap:** after aging, the total rank is at most `0.9 * max_age`, and the largest possible single rank is `0.9 * max_age`. Therefore any `_ZO_MAXAGE ∈ {0, 1}` **wipes the entire database on the next `add`** (`0.9*1 = 0.9 < 1.0`). Confirmed: `M=1` with `/big=100` → `count=0`; `M=2` → `/big = 1.7821782178217824` (= `100·0.9·2/101`); `M=3` → `/big = 2.6732673267326734`.

## 6. Timestamp behaviour of `add`

* **`add` ALWAYS sets `last_accessed = now`**, unconditionally, including overwriting a timestamp that is in the future: entry `("/x", 5.0, now+999999)` → after `add /x` it is `("/x", 6.0, now)` where `now == date +%s`.
* **Two `add`s of the same directory within the same second behave identically to any other pair of adds** — there is no de-duplication, no debounce, no "already added this second" shortcut. Two invocations inside one second: rank `1.0` then `2.0`, same timestamp both times. Three paths in one invocation (`add D D D`) → rank `3.0`.
* `query` never updates timestamps. `edit increment/decrement/delete/reload` never update timestamps. `remove` obviously not.
* `import --from z` copies the source timestamp verbatim; `import --from autojump` sets `last_accessed = 0` and rewrites rank as the logistic `1/(1+e^-rank)` (rank 5 → `0.9933071490757153`, rank 20000 → `1.0`).

## 7. Timestamp = Unix epoch seconds — confirmed

`add` wrote `1786337601` at the same instant `date +%s` printed `1786337601`. `date -u -d @1786338068` → `Mon Aug 10 05:01:08 UTC 2026`, matching the live `date -u`. The field is **u64**; see §1 (`0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`, `0x8000000000000000`, and i64 `-1000` all behave as "far future" → age 0 → ×4). `last_accessed = 0` gives age = `now` → the `/4` bucket. There is no special-casing of 0.

## 8. Consolidated pseudocode

```rust
const HOUR: u64 = 3_600; const DAY: u64 = 86_400; const WEEK: u64 = 604_800;

fn score(rank: f64, last_accessed: u64, now: u64) -> f64 {
    let d = now.saturating_sub(last_accessed);
    if      d < HOUR { rank * 4.0 }
    else if d < DAY  { rank * 2.0 }
    else if d < WEEK { rank / 2.0 }
    else             { rank / 4.0 }
}

fn print_score(w, score: f64, sep: char, term: char, path: &str) {
    write!(w, "{:>6.1}{sep}{path}{term}", score.clamp(0.0, 9999.0));
}
// query --list --score / query --score : sep = ' ',  term = '\n'
// edit <sub> / fzf stdin               : sep = '\t', term = '\0'

fn add(db, path, by: f64, now: u64) {          // by defaults to 1.0
    match db.iter_mut().find(|d| d.path == path) {
        Some(d) => { d.rank = f64::max(d.rank + by, 0.0); d.last_accessed = now; }
        None    => db.push(Dir { path, rank: f64::max(by, 0.0), last_accessed: now }),
    }
}

fn age(db, max_age: f64) {                     // called ONCE at the end of `add` only
    let mut sum = 0.0; for d in db.iter() { sum += d.rank; }   // db order, left to right
    if sum > max_age {
        let factor = 0.9 * max_age / sum;
        for i in (0..db.len()).rev() {
            db[i].rank *= factor;
            if db[i].rank < 1.0 { db.swap_remove(i); }
        }
    }
}
```

1. **`rank * 4.0` vs `rank / 0.25`, and `rank / 2.0` vs `rank * 0.5`** are bit-identical in IEEE-754; no experiment can distinguish which form the code uses. Same for `/4` vs `*0.25`.

3. **The exact source of `now`** (e.g. `SystemTime::now()` vs `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME)`) cannot be determined without tracing, which is prohibited. 4. **Whether the internal score-sort in `query` is literally `f64::total_cmp`** or a hand-rolled comparator producing the same total order — I verified the resulting order matches `total_cmp` exactly for `-NaN < -inf < finite < +inf < +NaN`, but any equivalent comparator is indistinguishable.

## 1. THE CORE ALGORITHM (validated by 500-case differential fuzz, 0 mismatches)

```
score(entry, now):
    age = now - entry.last_accessed          # seconds, i64
    if age <      3600 : return entry.rank * 4.0
    if age <     86400 : return entry.rank * 2.0
    if age <    604800 : return entry.rank * 0.5
    else               : return entry.rank * 0.25

query(db, keywords, base_dir, exclude_path, all, exclude_globs):
    now = current unix time
    # ONE sort over the WHOLE db, ascending by score, UNSTABLE (see §12)
    db.entries.sort_unstable_by(a,b -> total_cmp(score(a), score(b)))
    db.dirty = true                          # db file is ALWAYS rewritten, see §13

    for entry in reversed(db.entries):       # i.e. descending score
        if not matches_keywords(entry.path, keywords): continue
        if not matches_base_dir(entry.path, base_dir): continue
        if any(g.matches(entry.path) for g in exclude_globs):
            db.remove(entry); continue       # DESTRUCTIVE, see §13
        if exclude_path is not None and entry.path == exclude_path (byte-exact): continue
        if not all:
            md = (resolve_symlinks ? lstat : stat)(entry.path)
            if md is Err or not md.is_dir(): continue
        yield entry
        if not list_mode: break              # LAZY: stream stops at first hit

matches_keywords(path, keywords):
    if keywords is empty: return True
    p  = unicode_lowercase(path)             # Rust str::to_lowercase semantics
    ks = [unicode_lowercase(k) for k in keywords]
    last = ks[-1]
    idx = p.rfind(last)                      # rightmost occurrence; rfind("")==len(p)
    if idx is None: return False
    if '/' in p[idx+len(last):]: return False   # last kw must END in the final component
    p = p[:idx]                              # strictly before the last kw's START
    for k in reversed(ks[:-1]):
        i = p.rfind(k)
        if i is None: return False
        p = p[:i]
    return True

matches_base_dir(path, base):                # Rust Path::starts_with (component-wise)
    if base is None: return True
    return components(path)[:len(components(base))] == components(base)
```

`'/'` is the only separator recognized (`MAIN_SEPARATOR` on Linux). `'\'` is an ordinary character.

**There is NO match-quality scoring.** Ranking is purely frecency; how well/where the keywords matched contributes nothing.

## 2. Multiple keywords (probe 1)

Rules, all proven below:
1. Keywords must match **in order, left→right**.
2. Matches must be **strictly non-overlapping** (each earlier keyword must lie wholly before the *start* index of the next one's match).
3. Each keyword is a **contiguous literal substring** of the (lowercased) full path — including `/` characters, so a keyword may span components.
4. **The LAST keyword is special**: its match must *end* after the final `/`, i.e. it must end inside the basename. It may *start* anywhere before that (it can span the final separator). It does **not** need to equal the basename, nor be a prefix/suffix of it.
5. Non-final keywords have **no** basename restriction; they may match anywhere in the prefix.
6. Matching is right-to-left greedy (`rfind`), which is provably complete for “ordered non-overlapping substrings”, so this is equivalent to plain existence of such an assignment.

## 3. Case sensitivity (probe 2)

**Always case-insensitive. There is NO smartcase.** Both path and keywords are passed through Rust's full-Unicode `str::to_lowercase()`, then a byte-substring search is done.

```
$ zoxide query --list FOO   # identical output to `foo`, includes Foo, fOO, a/Foo, FooBar
$ zoxide query --list UPPER   -> /tmp/zw/T/UPPER
$ zoxide query --list upper   -> /tmp/zw/T/UPPER
$ zoxide query --list MIXEDCASE -> /tmp/zw/T/mixedCase
```

It is genuinely *lowercase-then-substring*, not per-char case-insensitive compare. Proof (Unicode special casing):

| dir in db | query | matches? | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `İstanbul` (U+0130) | `istanbul` | **NO** | `"İ".to_lowercase()` = `i` + U+0307 |
| `İstanbul` | `i̇stanbul` (i + U+0307) | YES | |
| `ΣΣΣ` | `σσσ` | **NO** | `"ΣΣΣ".to_lowercase()` = `σσς` (final-sigma rule) |
| `ΣΣΣ` | `ΣΣΣ` | YES | both sides lowercase to `σσς` |
| `ΣΣΣ` | `ςςς` | NO | |
| `ÄÖÜ` | `äöü` | YES | non-ASCII lowercasing is applied |
| `ǅ` (U+01C5 titlecase) | `ǆ`, `Ǆ`, `ǅ` | YES (all three) | |
| `STRASSE` | `straße` | NO | `ß` does not fold to `ss` in lowercase |
| `Straße` | `straße` | YES | |
| `日本語` | `日本語` | YES | |

The path **printed** is always the original, un-lowercased stored string.

## 4. Trailing slash semantics (probe 3)

There is no special "trailing slash" code path — it falls out of rule §2.4.

- **`foo/` (one keyword, trailing `/`)**: requires the literal substring `foo/` and it must end in the basename ⇒ the entry must be a **direct child of a component whose name ENDS with `foo`**.
  ```
  $ zoxide query --list foo/
  /tmp/zw/T/foo/bar
  /tmp/zw/T/fOO/BaR
  /tmp/zw/T/a/foo/bar
  /tmp/zw/T/a/Foo/bar
  ```
  Note `/tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub1` is **not** matched (`foo2/` ≠ `foo/`), but `2/` and `oo2/` do match it:
  ```
  $ zoxide query --list 2/    ->  /tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub2   /tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub1
  $ zoxide query --list a/    ->  /tmp/zw/T/a/foo  /tmp/zw/T/a/f o o  /tmp/zw/T/a/bar  /tmp/zw/T/a/b  /tmp/zw/T/a/Foo
  ```
  (`a/` yields only *direct* children of `…/a`; `a/foo/bar` is excluded because after `a/` there is another `/`.)
- **`foo /` (two keywords, last is `/`)** — the README's `z foo /`: `rfind("/")` always finds the **last** separator, so the check always passes and the remaining prefix is the **dirname**; then `foo` must occur anywhere in the dirname. Net effect: *"any entry that is at least one level below something matching foo"*.
  ```
  $ zoxide query --list foo /
  /tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub2
  /tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub1
  /tmp/zw/T/foo/bar
  /tmp/zw/T/fOO/BaR
  /tmp/zw/T/a/foo/bar
  /tmp/zw/T/a/Foo/bar
  ```
  So the README wording "subdirectory **starting with** foo" is wrong: it is "subdirectory of any path whose dirname *contains* foo". `/tmp/zw/T/foo` itself is excluded (its dirname `/tmp/zw/t` has no `foo`).
- **`/` alone** matches every entry (every abs path has a separator). `/ /` and `/ / /` also match everything with ≥2 / ≥3 separators.
- **`bar/`** matches only `/tmp/zw/T/a/bar/foo`.
- If a *stored* path itself ends with `/` (possible by hand-crafting the db), then `foo` does **not** match it but `foo/` does:
  ```
  db = { "/tmp/zw/T/foo/", "/tmp/zw/T/foo" }
  $ zoxide query --list --all foo    -> /tmp/zw/T/foo
  $ zoxide query --list --all foo/   -> /tmp/zw/T/foo/
  ```

## 6. `--base-dir` and "match after a prefix" (probes 5 & 9)

`--base-dir` is an **independent filter**; it does **not** re-root or trim the string that keywords are matched against. Keywords always match the **entire stored path**, including the part above the base dir. Decisive test:

```
db = { /tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub1, /tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub2, ... }
$ zoxide query --list --base-dir /tmp/zw/T/foo2 zw sub
/tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub2
/tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub1        # "zw" lives ABOVE the base dir and still counts
```
(`--base-dir /tmp/zw/T/foo2 T` and `… tmp` return nothing only because a *single* keyword must end in the basename.)

Exact `--base-dir` semantics — **Rust `Path::starts_with`, component-wise**, verified against a Python model over 15 base values with 0 mismatches:

| base-dir | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `/tmp/zw/T/a` | matches `/tmp/zw/T/a` **and** its descendants; **does not** match `/tmp/zw/T/abc` (component boundary required) |
| `/tmp/zw/T/a/`, `/tmp/zw/T/a//`, `//tmp/zw/T/a`, `/tmp/zw/T/./a`, `/tmp/./zw/T/a` | all identical to `/tmp/zw/T/a` (repeated/trailing separators and `.` components are ignored) |
| `/tmp/zw/T/a/../a` | matches **nothing** (`..` is a literal component, never resolved) |
| relative (`a`, `.`) | matches **nothing** — no canonicalisation, no cwd resolution |
| `/tmp/zw/t/a` | matches nothing — base-dir comparison is **case-SENSITIVE** (unlike keywords) |
| `""` (empty) | matches everything |
| `/` | matches everything |
| nonexistent dir | no error; simply filters by string prefix (`--base-dir /tmp/zw/NOPE` → empty, exit 0) |

The base dir **itself can be returned**:
```
$ zoxide query --list --base-dir /tmp/zw/T/a   # last line of output is /tmp/zw/T/a
$ zoxide query --list --base-dir /tmp/zw/T/foo foo   -> /tmp/zw/T/foo
```
`--base-dir` may be given only once (clap: `cannot be used multiple times`).

## 8. Availability filtering, `--all`, files vs. missing (probe 7)

The availability check is `metadata(path)?.is_dir()` (default) or `symlink_metadata(path)?.is_dir()` when `_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS=1`.

```
db(rank): nonexistent_x=9, afile=8 (a regular FILE), deleted_dir=7, onlydb=6 (rmdir'ed), foo=3
$ zoxide query --list --score
  12.0 /tmp/zw/T/foo
$ zoxide query --list --score --all
  36.0 /tmp/zw/T/nonexistent_x
  32.0 /tmp/zw/T/afile
  28.0 /tmp/zw/T/deleted_dir
  24.0 /tmp/zw/T/onlydb
  12.0 /tmp/zw/T/foo
```
- **"does not exist" and "exists but is a regular file" are treated identically** — both filtered out without `--all`, both shown with `--all`. No distinct message, no distinct behaviour.
- Entries for nonexistent dirs / files are **NOT deleted** by a query. The entry count stayed at 5 before and after (`python3 /tmp/zw/rddb.py …` → `version=3 count=5`). *(The only thing that deletes is `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS`, §10.)*
- Relative paths stored in the db are stat'ed **relative to the cwd**:
  ```
  db = { "foo", "T/foo", "./rel/foo", "/tmp/zw/T/foo/", "" }
  (cd /tmp/zw && query --list foo)  -> ./rel/foo   T/foo
  (cd /       && query --list foo)  -> (empty)
  ```
- Symlinks:
  ```
  db = { symok -> realdir(dir), symbad -> dangling, symfile -> a file, realdir }
  default              -> /tmp/zw/T/realdir, /tmp/zw/T/symok
  _ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS=1 -> /tmp/zw/T/realdir            # symlinks are NEVER returned
  --all                -> realdir, symfile, symbad, symok
  ```
- `--all` skips *only* the availability check; keyword, base-dir, `--exclude` and `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS` filters still apply.
- Duplicate paths in the db are **not** de-duplicated: 3 entries for `/tmp/zw/T/foo` produce 3 output lines.

## 9. `--exclude <path>` (probe 8)

- **Exact, byte-for-byte string equality** against the stored path. No canonicalisation, no glob, no prefix/subdir semantics.
- Given **at most once**: `--exclude a --exclude b` → `error: the argument '--exclude <path>' cannot be used multiple times`, exit **2**. Missing value → `error: a value is required for '--exclude <path>' but none was supplied`, exit **2**.
- Does **not** exclude subdirectories: `--exclude /tmp/zw/T/foo` + query `bar` still returns `/tmp/zw/T/foo/bar`.
- Any deviation in the string breaks it (all of these fail to exclude `/tmp/zw/T/foo`): `/tmp/zw/T/foo/`, `/tmp/zw/T//foo`, `/tmp/zw/T/./foo`, `/tmp/zw/t/foo`, `/tmp/zw/T/a/../foo`, relative `foo` (run from `/tmp/zw/T`), `''`.
- Conversely, if the *stored* path is `/tmp/zw/T/foo/`, then `--exclude '/tmp/zw/T/foo/'` **does** exclude it — confirming raw string compare, not `Path` compare.
- It does **not** delete anything from the db (count 50 → 50).
- This is what the shell wrapper uses: `zoxide query --exclude "$(__zoxide_pwd)" -- "$@"` where `__zoxide_pwd` is `\builtin pwd -L`. Without it, the cwd **is** returned by `query`.

## 10. `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS` — the destructive filter (surprise finding)

`_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS` is applied by `query` (not just by `add`) and **permanently DELETES matching entries from `db.zo`**.

```
$ python3 /tmp/zw/mkdb.py /tmp/zw/F1/db.zo < /tmp/zw/paths.tsv        # 50 entries
$ _ZO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/zw/F1 _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS='/tmp/zw/T/foo*' /workspace/executable query --list foo
/tmp/zw/T/fOO
/tmp/zw/T/barfoo
/tmp/zw/T/a/foo
/tmp/zw/T/a/bar/foo
/tmp/zw/T/a/Foo
/tmp/zw/T/FooBar
/tmp/zw/T/Foo
$ python3 /tmp/zw/rddb.py /tmp/zw/F1/db.zo | head -1
version=3 count=42          # /tmp/zw/T/{foo,foo2,foo3,foobar} were REMOVED from disk
```

Properties:
- Separator between globs is **`:`** (Unix `PATH` style). `;` is not a separator (it becomes part of a single literal glob and matches nothing).
- Syntax is the Rust `glob` crate `Pattern` with **default `MatchOptions`**, matching the **whole** path:
  - `case_sensitive = true` → `/tmp/zw/T/?oo` removes `Foo` and `foo` but nothing else; `/tmp/zw/T/foo*` does not touch `/tmp/zw/T/fOO`.
  - `require_literal_separator = false` → **`*` crosses `/`**: `/tmp/zw/T/*` removes all 50 entries including `/tmp/zw/T/a/foo/bar`; `*foo*` removes every path containing `foo` at any depth.
  - `require_literal_leading_dot = false` → `/tmp/zw/T/*` also removes `/tmp/zw/T/.hidden`.
  - `[abc]` ranges work; `[!f]*` is negation; `[^f]` is a *literal* class of `^` and `f`.
- Invalid pattern → exit **1**, stderr exactly:
  ```
  zoxide: invalid glob in _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS: [
  
  Caused by:
      Pattern syntax error near position 0: invalid range pattern
  ```
- **Deletion is lazy and filter-ordered.** An entry is deleted only if the stream actually reaches it, i.e. only if it *passes* the keyword filter **and** the base-dir filter:
  - keyword filter first: `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS=/tmp/zw/T/zz` + `query --list k` leaves `zz` in the db (count 4 → 4).
  - base-dir before glob: `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS=/tmp/zw/T/foo` + `query --list --base-dir /tmp/zw/T/a foo` leaves `/tmp/zw/T/foo` in the db.
  - glob check is before the existence check and before `--exclude`: a nonexistent, glob-matching, keyword-matching entry is deleted; `--all` does not prevent it; `--exclude`-ing the same path does not prevent it.
  - non-`--list` queries stop at the first result, so lower-scoring glob-matching entries survive:
    ```
    db ranks: ka=9, zz=7, kb=5, kc=1 ; _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS='/tmp/zw/T/k[bc]'
    query k        -> /tmp/zw/T/ka   ; db still has ka,zz,kb,kc  (4 entries)
    query --list k -> /tmp/zw/T/ka   ; db now has ka,zz only     (2 entries)
    ```

## 11. Zero keywords / empty keywords (probe 10)

- **Zero keywords** (`query --list`) → `matches_keywords` returns `true` immediately → **every** entry (subject to base-dir / excludes / availability), in descending score order. `query` with no keywords prints the single top entry, exit 0. `query -i` with no keywords is allowed (no clap error).
- **Empty-string keyword** `""` matches everything: `rfind("")` returns `len(p)`, the "no separator after" test looks at `p[len:]` = `""`, and the prefix handed to the next keyword is the *whole* path unchanged. Consequences:
  - `query --list ''` ≡ `query --list` (all entries).
  - `query --list foo ''` = "`foo` anywhere in the full path, **no basename restriction**" — 17 hits including `/tmp/zw/T/foo2/sub1` and `/tmp/zw/T/a/foo/bar`.
  - `query --list '' foo` ≡ `query --list foo`.
  - `query --list foo '' bar` ≡ `query --list foo bar` (byte-identical output).
  - `'' ''` ≡ all entries.

## 13. Sort order and tie-breaking (probe 12)

- Key = `score(entry, now)` (see §1). The whole db is sorted **ascending** with an **unstable** comparison sort (`sort_unstable_by` + `total_cmp`-like ordering), and results are emitted by iterating the sorted array **in reverse** ⇒ output is **descending score**.
- `total_cmp` ordering is confirmed by NaN placement: ranks `{-5, 0, +inf, NaN}` are stored back as `[-5, 0, inf, NaN]` (ascending) and printed as `NaN, 9999.0(inf), 0.0, 0.0` (descending) — NaN sorts **above** `+inf`.
- **Ties**: the order is *unspecified* but **deterministic** for identical input (two runs from the same db byte-for-byte produced identical output).
  - For a db with **≤ 32 total entries**, the sort behaves stably, so equal-score entries come out in **exact reverse of the db file order**. Verified for n = 4, 10, 20, 21, 22, 30, 31, 32 with two interleaved score groups, and for a 46-entry-all-equal case (`query --list foo` output was the exact reverse of db order).
  - From **33 total entries upward** the tie order is a scrambled (but reproducible) permutation. Verified: n = 33…39, 40, 50, 64, 80, 100, 128, 200 all scramble; n = 32 does not. Example (n=200, all ranks equal → still unscrambled because pdqsort's all-equal fast path applies; n=200 with two interleaved rank values → scrambled).
  - The threshold is on **total db entries**, not on the number of matches: a 100-entry db where only 10 entries match still yields scrambled ties (`009 001 005 007 003 000 008 006 004 002` instead of `009 007 005 003 001 008 006 004 002 000`).
- **Side effect:** `query` **always rewrites `db.zo`** (new inode each time, atomic temp+rename), storing the entries in the sorted-ascending order. Confirmed even when the content is unchanged:
  ```
  $ stat -c 'ino=%i mtime=%Y' /tmp/zw/D4/db.zo ; zoxide query --list >/dev/null ; stat -c 'ino=%i mtime=%Y' /tmp/zw/D4/db.zo
  ino=84414744 mtime=1786336752
  ino=84415189 mtime=1786336799
  ```
  The db-after order is exactly the reverse of the query output order (verified byte-for-byte on a 200-entry db).
- `_ZO_MAXAGE` has **no effect** on `query` (no aging/pruning happens at query time; an 8-entry db with `_ZO_MAXAGE=1` stayed at 8 entries).

--nth=2
--read0
--exact
--no-sort
--bind=ctrl-z:ignore,btab:up,tab:down

--keep-right
--border=sharp
--height=45%

## 15. Reference reimplementation (drop-in)

```python
SEP = '/'

def score(rank, last_accessed, now):
    age = now - last_accessed
    if age < 3600:   return rank * 4.0
    if age < 86400:  return rank * 2.0
    if age < 604800: return rank * 0.5
    return rank * 0.25

def matches_keywords(path, keywords):
    if not keywords: return True
    p  = path.lower()                        # Rust str::to_lowercase
    ks = [k.lower() for k in keywords]
    last = ks[-1]
    i = p.rfind(last)
    if i < 0: return False
    if SEP in p[i+len(last):]: return False
    p = p[:i]
    for k in reversed(ks[:-1]):
        j = p.rfind(k)
        if j < 0: return False
        p = p[:j]
    return True

def components(s):                            # Rust Path::components, unix, abs paths
    out = ['/'] if s.startswith('/') else []
    out += [c for c in s.split('/') if c not in ('', '.')]
    return out

def matches_base_dir(path, base):
    if base is None: return True
    a, b = components(path), components(base)
    return a[:len(b)] == b

def query(db, keywords, now, *, base_dir=None, exclude=None,
          all_=False, list_=False, resolve_symlinks=False, exclude_globs=()):
    db.sort(key=lambda e: score(e.rank, e.ts, now))   # ascending, ties unspecified
    out, deleted = [], []
    for e in reversed(db):
        if not matches_keywords(e.path, keywords): continue
        if not matches_base_dir(e.path, base_dir): continue
        if any(g.matches_whole(e.path) for g in exclude_globs):   # case-sensitive, * crosses /
            deleted.append(e); continue
        if exclude is not None and e.path == exclude: continue    # byte-exact
        if not all_:
            st = lstat_or_none(e.path) if resolve_symlinks else stat_or_none(e.path)
            if st is None or not st.is_dir(): continue
        out.append(e)
        if not list_: break
    for e in deleted: db.remove(e)
    save(db)                                   # always rewritten, sorted ascending
    return out                                 # already descending by score
```

## 1. Location of the database

| Condition | Resolved data dir | DB file |
|---|---|---|
| `_ZO_DATA_DIR=<abs path>` | `<abs path>` | `<abs path>/db.zo` |
| `_ZO_DATA_DIR` unset, `XDG_DATA_HOME=<abs path>` | `<XDG_DATA_HOME>/zoxide` | `<XDG_DATA_HOME>/zoxide/db.zo` |
| `_ZO_DATA_DIR` unset, `XDG_DATA_HOME` unset/empty/relative | `$HOME/.local/share/zoxide` | `$HOME/.local/share/zoxide/db.zo` |
| `_ZO_DATA_DIR` and `HOME` both unset | falls back to the passwd entry (`getpwuid`) home — as root: `/root/.local/share/zoxide` | `/root/.local/share/zoxide/db.zo` |

- The filename is **always exactly `db.zo`**. No other persistent file is ever created (no lock file, no journal, no `.bak`). The only other file that can appear is a `tmp_*` write temp (§5).
- `XDG_DATA_HOME=` (empty) and `XDG_DATA_HOME=relpath` are both **ignored** (fall through to `$HOME/.local/share`). Verified:
  `env -u _ZO_DATA_DIR HOME=/tmp/probe/h4 XDG_DATA_HOME= /workspace/executable add /tmp` → creates `/tmp/probe/h4/.local/share/zoxide/db.zo`.

  ```

- The same error appears when the *derived default* path is not absolute, e.g. `HOME=h5` (relative) with `_ZO_DATA_DIR`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` unset → `zoxide: _ZO_DATA_DIR must be an absolute path`, exit 1. (Yes — the message names `_ZO_DATA_DIR` even though `_ZO_DATA_DIR` was not set.)

### Directory creation
The data directory is created **recursively** (`mkdir -p` semantics) by every db‑touching subcommand, *before* reading, and **regardless of whether anything is later written**:

| command | data dir created? | `db.zo` created? | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query -l` (nonexistent dir) | yes | **yes (12 bytes)** | 0 |
| `add /nonexistent` | yes | no | 1 |
| `remove` (no args) | yes | no | 0 |
| `remove /nope` | yes | no | 1 |
| `init bash` | **no** | no | 0 |

Permissions: directories are created with mode `0777 & ~umask`, `db.zo` with `0666 & ~umask`. Verified:
- `umask 000` → dir `drwxrwxrwx`, file `-rw-rw-rw-`
- `umask 022` → dir `drwxr-xr-x`, file `-rw-r--r--`
- `umask 027` → dir `drwxr-x---`, file `-rw-r-----`
- `umask 077` → dir `drwx------`, file `-rw-------`

Overwriting does **not** preserve the old file's mode: `chmod 600 db.zo` then `add` → file becomes `0644` (umask 022). A `0444` `db.zo` is silently replaced as long as the *directory* is writable.

Failure to create the directory:
```

Caused by:
    Permission denied (os error 13)
```
exit **1**.

## 2. Byte layout

Little‑endian throughout, **no padding, no alignment**. This is bincode 1.x with fixed‑int encoding.

```
offset  size  type      field
------  ----  --------  --------------------------------------
0x00      4   u32 LE    version                (0.9.9 writes 3)
0x04      8   u64 LE    entry_count (N)
        --- repeated N times, contiguously ---
+0        8   u64 LE    path_byte_len (L)      (BYTE length, not chars)
+8        L   bytes     path (UTF-8, no NUL terminator)
+8+L      8   f64 LE    rank        (IEEE-754 binary64)
+16+L     8   i64 LE    last_accessed (Unix seconds, signed)
```

**File size = 12 + Σ (24 + byte_len(path_i))**. Verified against a 3,000,000‑entry file: `12 + 3000000*(24+48) = 216000012` bytes exactly.

Field order is confirmed as **path, rank, timestamp** (not rank‑first).

Notes:
- Path length is byte length. `/tmp/probe/dirs/日本語` → `L = 0x19 = 25`.
- Timestamp is seconds (not ms/ns) — an entry added at wall clock `2026-08-10 04:35:53Z` stored `1786336553`.
- The version field is read **separately** from the first 4 bytes; the remainder (`bytes[4..]`) is bincode‑deserialized as a `Vec<Entry>` **from a slice** (whole file is read into memory — proven by the "Slice had bytes remaining" error).

## 3. Version field

0.9.9 writes **`03 00 00 00`** (u32 LE = 3), always, regardless of what version was read (a v3 file is the only thing it will read anyway).

Any version ≠ 3 (tested 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 255, 65535, 4294967295, 7):
```
zoxide: unsupported version (got <N>, supports 3)
```
exit **1**. Byte‑exact for N=7 (48 bytes): `zoxide: unsupported version (got 7, supports 3)\n`.

The version check runs **before** the payload is parsed: a 4‑byte file `00 00 00 00` yields `unsupported version (got 0, supports 3)`, not a truncation error.

env _ZO_DATA_DIR=$D /workspace/executable add /tmp; echo $?
```

## 5. How the file is written (atomic rename + temp files)

Write algorithm (fully confirmed):

1. `mkdir -p` the data dir.
2. Read whole `db.zo` into memory (tolerating `ENOENT` only).
3. If the in‑memory db was modified, **canonicalize** the db path, create a temp file **in the parent of the canonicalized path** named `tmp_` + 12 random chars, write the whole serialized db, then `rename(temp, db_path)`.

**Temp filename pattern: `tmp_XXXXXXXXXXXX`** — literal prefix `tmp_` (4 bytes) plus exactly **12** characters drawn uniformly from `[0-9A-Za-z]` (62 symbols). Total length 16. 40 samples collected, all length 16, alphabet exactly `0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`. Examples: `tmp_Ol2mCApRqSCa`, `tmp_S0T42SBJ4Kzi`, `tmp_bptn9yqsQI6Z`, `tmp_PEG57GLDw0vq`.
Temp file mode is `0666 & ~umask` (observed `0o100644` with umask 022) — **not** 0600.

Ways to observe it:
- **Read‑only data dir (non‑root):** the creation error prints the temp name.
  ```sh
  chmod 555 $DIR; setpriv --reuid=1000 --regid=1000 --clear-groups \
      env _ZO_DATA_DIR=$DIR /workspace/executable add /tmp
  # zoxide: could not write to database
  # Caused by:
  #     0: could not create file: /tmp/probe/ro/data/tmp_Ol2mCApRqSCa
  #     1: Permission denied (os error 13)
  ```
- **Poll during a slow write** with a 3M‑entry (216 MB) db: `os.listdir` shows `['db.zo', 'tmp_1i3wxFgEsNR0']`.

**Atomicity is real.** Polling `stat(db.zo)` continuously during a write over a 216 MB db observed only two states — `(ino=84422152, size=12)` then `(ino=84448584, size=56)`; never a partial/missing file. The inode always changes.

**Temp cleanup:** on *any* error after creation (write failure, rename failure) the temp file is **removed**; the original `db.zo` is left byte‑intact. The only way to leave a temp behind is to kill the process:
```sh
# 4M-entry db, SIGKILL as soon as tmp_ appears
# result: ['db.zo' 288000012, 'tmp_nVlc5nsFj2Y0' 288000057]
```
Stale `tmp_*` files are **never** cleaned up by later runs (verified: a hand‑placed `tmp_AAAAAAAAAAAA` survives an `add`).

**Symlink behaviour (surprising, and it differs by target existence):**
- `db.zo` is a symlink to an **existing** file → the path is canonicalized: the temp file is created in the *target's* directory and renamed onto the target. The symlink is preserved. Observed temp at `/tmp/probe/symt/tmp_FCIJz92EKN3z` while `_ZO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/probe/symd`.
- `db.zo` is a **dangling** symlink → canonicalization fails, the literal path is used, and `rename` **replaces the symlink with a regular file**; the target is never created.

### Does it write when nothing changed?
**Yes for every `query`, no for read‑only paths.** `db.zo` is rewritten (new inode, new mtime, byte‑identical content) on *every* `query` invocation — including `query` with no match (exit 1) and `query -l` on a 1‑entry or 0‑entry db — because query sorts the entry vector in place and marks the db dirty.

| command | rewrites `db.zo`? |
|---|---|
| `add <dir>` (success) | yes |
| `add <bad path>` (any arg invalid) | **no** — validated first, nothing written |
| `add` on a dir matching `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS` | **no** — complete no‑op, `db.zo` not even created |
| `query` / `query -l` / `query -i` / no‑match query | **yes, always** |
| `remove <path>` success | yes |
| `remove <path>` not found | **no** |
| `remove` (no args) | **no** |
| `import` (with `--merge` or into empty db) | yes |
| `edit` (interactive, even with empty fzf selection) | yes |
| `edit reload` | **no** (read‑only) |
| `edit increment/decrement/delete <path>` | yes |
| `init <shell>` | no (never touches the data dir) |

## 6. Locking / concurrency

**There is no locking of any kind.** Semantics are read‑modify‑write with last‑writer‑wins.

- 60 concurrent `add` processes against one fresh db → **2 entries survive**, reproducibly (3 runs: 2, 2, 2). Sequential control with the same 60 dirs → 60 entries.
  ```sh
  D=$(mktemp -d); for i in $(seq 1 60); do env _ZO_DATA_DIR=$D /workspace/executable add /tmp/probe/many/d$i & done; wait
  ```
- Holding an exclusive `flock(LOCK_EX)` on `db.zo` from another process does **not** block zoxide: it completes in 0.01 s, rc 0. So no `flock`/`fcntl` locking.
- No lock file is ever created in the data dir.
- No temp files leak from concurrent runs (each uses a distinct random name and cleans up).

## 7. Entry ordering in the file

- **`add` appends** new entries at the end; incrementing an existing entry does **not** move it. Order after `add a; add b; add c; add b` is `a, b, c`.
- **`add` increments only the FIRST matching entry** if duplicates exist in the file.
- **`remove` uses swap‑remove**: the last entry is moved into the removed slot. `[alpha,beta,gamma,delta]` − `beta` → `[alpha,delta,gamma]`; then − `alpha` → `[gamma,delta]`.
- **`query` (any form) sorts the whole vector ASCENDING by *aged score* and persists that order.** Printed output is the reverse (descending). The comparator behaves like `f64::total_cmp`: `-NaN` sorts first, `+NaN` sorts last, `-inf` first, `+inf` near-last.
  - Score, not raw rank, is the key: `/tmp` rank 10 ts=now−10 days (score 2.5) sorts *before* `/usr` rank 3 ts=now (score 12).
- **`import`** (both `--from z` and `--from autojump`) leaves the db **sorted ascending by path bytes** and de‑duplicated by path (ranks summed, timestamp = max). `/zz|1|100`, `/zz|2|200`, `/aa|3|300` → `[/aa rank 3.0 ts 300, /zz rank 3.0 ts 200]`.
- **Aging** (`_ZO_MAXAGE`) preserves relative order (retain‑in‑place).
- The `edit` fzf feed and `edit reload` output are descending by score, NUL‑separated, format `%6.1f\t%s\0`; they do not change stored order.

Score/age multipliers that drive the stored order (measured with rank 100):

| age = now − ts | multiplier |
|---|---|
| `< 3600 s` (incl. future timestamps) | ×4 → 400.0 |
| `[3600, 86400)` | ×2 → 200.0 |
| `[86400, 604800)` | ×0.5 → 50.0 |
| `>= 604800` | ×0.25 → 25.0 |

Negative timestamps are treated as **far‑future** (age 0, ×4) — presumably `ts as u64`. `ts = -5` → score 4.0 for rank 1.0; `ts = i64::MAX` → 4.0; `ts = 0` → 25.0 for rank 100.

`query -s` display clamps to `[0.0, 9999.0]` (`-inf`/`-3.0` → `0.0`; `+inf`/`1e308` → `9999.0`; `NaN` → `NaN`) but the **stored rank is untouched**. Format is `%6.1f` + one space + path + `\n` (e.g. `<SP><SP><SP>4.0<SP>/tmp\n`, 12 bytes).

### Aging (affects the file contents on `add`)
Triggered only by `add`/`import` paths, **never** by `query`. When the total of all ranks (after applying the increment) is **strictly greater** than `_ZO_MAXAGE` (default **10000**):
```
factor = 0.9 * MAXAGE / total_rank
every rank *= factor
entries with rank < 1.0 are deleted (rank == 1.0 is KEPT)
```
Verified numerically: `{/x:9.5}` + add(1.0), MAXAGE=10 → total 10.5, factor 0.857142857… → `/x` = 8.142857142857142, the new entry (0.857) deleted. Total exactly 10 → no aging. Default: total 10000 → no aging; total 10001 → `10000 * 0.9*10000/10001 = 8999.100089991001`.
Boundary proof for the ≥1.0 retention: `{/x:177, /y:2}` + add(1.0), MAXAGE=100 → total 180, factor exactly 0.5 → `/y` = **1.0 survives**, added entry (0.5) deleted.
`_ZO_MAXAGE=0` wipes the db to 0 entries (exit 0). `_ZO_MAXAGE=abc` or `-5`:
```
zoxide: unable to parse _ZO_MAXAGE as integer: abc

Caused by:
    invalid digit found in string
```
exit 1.

## 8. Empty database

Yes — the empty db is written to disk. Running `query -l` in a fresh `_ZO_DATA_DIR` creates the directory and a **12‑byte** `db.zo`:

```
0000000 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
        ^^ version = 3        ^^ count = 0
```

A db that becomes empty (last entry removed, or wiped by aging) is written as those same 12 bytes. Re‑running `query -l` on a 12‑byte db rewrites it to the identical 12 bytes with a **new inode**.

## Additional facts relevant to a reimplementation

- **Paths written by zoxide are always absolute, normalized, and valid UTF‑8.** Trailing `/` stripped, `..`/`.` resolved lexically, relative args resolved against cwd. Symlinks are **not** resolved unless `_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS=1` (then `/tmp/probe/symlink` is stored as `/tmp/probe/symtarget`).
- `add` requires each argument to be an existing **directory**; a regular file or missing path gives `zoxide: not a directory: <path>` and exit 1, with **no** db write even if other args were valid (validation is all‑or‑nothing).
- Non‑UTF‑8 argument: `zoxide: invalid unicode in path: /tmp/probe/bad<U+FFFD>` (lossy‑rendered), exit 1. So zoxide itself can never emit invalid UTF‑8 into the db.
- `add` default increment is `1.0`; `-s/--score <F>` sets the initial rank for a new entry and is **added** to the rank of an existing one (`rank 2.0` + `-s 3` → `5.0`). The incremented entry's timestamp is set to now; other entries' timestamps are untouched.
- `query` **never** prunes entries whose directory no longer exists (it only filters them from output unless `--all`).
- `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS` matches during query and **permanently deletes** the matching entries from the db (via swap‑remove). The `--exclude <path>` CLI flag only filters output and does not modify the db.
- Hidden `edit` subcommands that mutate the db: `zoxide edit reload` (read‑only), `zoxide edit increment <path>`, `zoxide edit decrement <path>`, `zoxide edit delete <path>`. Decrement floors at 0.0 without deleting.

Missing import file: `zoxide: could not open database for importing: /nope/nope\n\nCaused by:\n    No such file or directory (os error 2)\n`, exit 1.
- A 3,000,000‑entry / 216 MB database round‑trips correctly (whole file is buffered in memory).

## 3. `query --score` (`-s`)

Works both with and without `--list`. Column format is exactly:

```
{score:>6.1}<SP>{path}<LF>
```

i.e. **Rust `format!("{:>6.1}", score)`, then one single space, then the path**. Width 6, right-aligned with spaces, exactly 1 fraction digit, round-half-to-even (Rust float formatting).

```
9999.0 /tmp/.../dirs/sp ace
   4.0 /tmp/.../dirs/alpha
   2.0 /tmp/.../dirs/alphabeta
   0.5 /tmp/.../dirs/beta
   0.2 /tmp/.../dirs/gamma/delta
   0.0 /tmp/.../dirs/zed
```

`--score` without `--list` prints exactly one line (the top match) in the same format, exit 0; no match → exit 1 + `zoxide: no match found<LF>`.

### Score function (measured exactly)

`score = rank * f(age)` where `age = now - last_accessed` (seconds):

| age | multiplier |
|---|---|
| `age < 3600` (including negative / future timestamps) | **× 4** |
| `3600 <= age < 86400` | **× 2** |
| `86400 <= age < 604800` | **× 0.5** |
| `age >= 604800` | **× 0.25** |

Boundaries verified exactly at 3599/3600, 86399/86400, 604799/604800 (`rank=1.0` → `4.0 / 2.0`, `2.0 / 0.5`, `0.5 / 0.2`).

### Clamping / special values (all measured)

- Displayed score is clamped to **[0.0, 9999.0]**: `rank=2500.0` (→10000.0) prints `9999.0`; `rank=2499.875` (→9999.5) prints `9999.0`; `rank=2499.625` (→9998.5) prints `9998.5`.
- Negative → `   0.0` (`rank=-3.0` → `   0.0`).
- `+inf` → `9999.0`; `-inf` → `   0.0`.
- `NaN` → literal `   NaN` (3 chars right-padded to width 6). NaN entries also break the sort ordering (a NaN entry appeared first in output).
- **`-0.0` is NOT clamped to `0.0`** — it prints `  -0.0` (4 chars, width 6). Repro: entry with `rank = -0.0` → line `  -0.0 /tmp/.../dirs/alpha`.
- Rounding: `0.05` → `0.1`; exact `0.25` → `0.2` (round-half-to-even).

## 8. Does `query` modify the database? — **YES, ALWAYS**

`query` **unconditionally rewrites `db.zo`** on every invocation that gets past argument parsing:

- Rewritten via **temp file + rename**: the inode changes (`84415259` → `84415262`), and the temp file is named **`tmp_` + 12 random `[A-Za-z0-9]` chars** in the data dir (observed: `tmp_9lTs4GGp0sRm`, `tmp_Juqrl6ffhad0`, `tmp_r1cH1k8xlJWA`, `tmp_IQKfu6pQKKyx`, `tmp_Csv4G6w1KHco`, `tmp_4vI97cIkuJnT`).
- **mtime always changes**, even when the resulting bytes are byte-identical (already-sorted db, md5 unchanged, mtime changed — verified over two consecutive runs).
- **Content change: entries are reordered to ascending-by-score** (a stable sort; equal-score entries keep their relative on-disk order). Ranks, timestamps and paths are otherwise untouched, and `f64` bit patterns are preserved exactly (`0.1`, `1/3`, `1e-300`, `π`, `1e-320`, `-0.0`, `NaN`, `±inf` all round-tripped).
- If `db.zo` / the data dir does not exist, `query` **creates the directory tree recursively and writes a 12-byte empty db** (`03 00 00 00` + `00×8`) — even on the no-match path.
- Happens for: match, no match, `--list`, `--score`, `--all`, `-i` success, `-i` with fzf missing, `-i` with fzf exit 1/2/128/**130**. Verified in each case.
- **Timing: the write happens AFTER fzf exits.** A fake fzf that `stat`s `db.zo` sees the *pre*-run mtime and md5; the file changes only after fzf returns.
- **The write happens AFTER stdout is produced, and its failure is fatal.** Running as an unprivileged user (`setpriv --reuid=1000`) against a mode-`555` data dir: all 5 paths are printed to stdout, then exit **1** with:
```
zoxide: could not write to database

Caused by:
    0: could not create file: /tmp/.../ro4/tmp_Juqrl6ffhad0
    1: Permission denied (os error 13)
```
- `_ZO_MAXAGE` has **no effect** on `query` (with `_ZO_MAXAGE=10` and total rank 200.5, no aging/decay/deletion occurred; ranks and count unchanged).
- No deduplication and no pruning of nonexistent directories occurs during this rewrite (entry counts unchanged in both cases).

## 9. `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS` and `_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS`

### `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS` — **YES, `query` honours it**

- Split on `:` (Linux). Each element is a **glob** (`glob` crate `Pattern`), matched against the whole stored path.
- `*` **crosses `/`** (`require_literal_separator: false`): `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="$W/dirs/*"` excluded `…/dirs/gamma/delta` as well as the direct children — all 5 entries vanished.
- `?` (single char) and `[ab]` character classes work: `…/dirs/alph?` removed `alpha` only; `…/dirs/[ab]*` removed `alpha`, `alphabeta`, `beta`.
- **Case-sensitive**: `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="$W/DIRS/alpha"` excluded nothing.
- Exact-path element matches only that path (`…/dirs` and `…/dirs/` exclude nothing; no implicit subtree exclusion).
- Applies to `--list`, to the single-match path, and **also with `--all`**.
- If everything is excluded: `--list` → empty + exit 0; plain `query` → exit 1 `zoxide: no match found`.
- **Default when unset is `$HOME` (exact, not a subtree)** and it *is* enforced by `query`: with `HOME=$W/fakehome`, `$W/fakehome` was omitted from `--list` while `$W/fakehome/sub` was kept. Setting `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS=` (empty) or `:` disables all exclusions (both `$W/fakehome` and `$W/fakehome/sub` appear).
- Invalid glob → exit **1**, stderr:
```
zoxide: invalid glob in _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS: [

Caused by:
    Pattern syntax error near position 0: invalid range pattern
```
(120 bytes; note the offending pattern is echoed after `: `.)

### `_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS` — **NO effect on `query`**

`_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS=1` produced byte-identical output in every test, including a db containing both `$W/thelink/real` (via symlink) and `$W/link_target/real` (real path): both are listed, unmerged, in both modes. Symlinked directories that resolve are treated as existing; **dangling** symlinks are treated as nonexistent (hidden unless `--all`).

### `_ZO_ECHO` — no effect on `query`

`_ZO_ECHO=0`, `1`, `yes` all produce identical output (it only affects the generated shell functions).

## 10. `--exclude` and `--base-dir` (CLI flags, for completeness)

- `--exclude <path>`: **exact string comparison, no globbing, no path normalization.** `--exclude "$W/dirs/alpha"` drops that entry; `--exclude "$W/dirs/alpha/"` (trailing slash) drops **nothing**; `--exclude alpha` (relative) drops nothing; `--exclude "$W/dirs/*"` drops nothing. May be given **at most once** (second use → clap "cannot be used multiple times", exit 2). Applies with `--all` too.
- `--base-dir <path>`: **component-wise prefix filter** (not a raw string prefix). `--base-dir "$W/dirs/alpha"` matched `…/dirs/alpha` but **not** `…/dirs/alphaX`. Trailing slash is tolerated (`…/alpha/` behaves like `…/alpha`). A relative value (`dirs`) or one containing `..` (`$W/dirs/../dirs`) matches nothing (no canonicalization). An empty value (`--base-dir ""`) matches everything. A nonexistent directory is not an error — it just yields no candidates (`--list` → empty, exit 0; plain `query` → exit 1).
- `--base-dir` and `--exclude` compose (both applied).

## 11. TTY vs non-TTY

Compared `script -qc '…' /dev/null` (pty on stdin/stdout/stderr) against plain pipes:

- `query alpha`: identical bytes (`…/dirs/alpha` + `\n`; the `\r` seen in the pty capture is added by the pty line discipline, not by zoxide). Exit 0 both ways.
- `query --list`: identical, one path per line. Exit 0 both ways.
- No match: identical `zoxide: no match found`, exit 1 both ways.
- **Interactive mode is NEVER auto-enabled.** `query` on a TTY does not spawn fzf; only explicit `-i`/`--interactive` does. Conversely, `-i` works fine with **no TTY at all** — zoxide does not check for a terminal, does not refuse, and does not pass anything different to fzf (argc=16 in both cases).
- Non-interactive `query` **does not read stdin at all**: `printf 'line1\nline2\n' | { executable query --list >/dev/null; cat; }` still printed `line1\nline2`.
- No color/escape sequences are ever emitted by `query` itself in either mode (zoxide only sets `CLICOLOR*` for the fzf child).
- Output is not line-buffered-vs-block-buffered visible: `query --list | head -1` with 200,000 entries exits **0** with empty stderr (EPIPE/SIGPIPE swallowed); `query --list >&-` (closed stdout) also exits **0** with empty stderr. Full run without `head` emits exactly 200,000 lines.

## 12. Keyword matching semantics (measured, since it drives what `--list` prints)

DB: `…/mm/Foo`, `…/mm/foobar`, `…/mm/bar/foo`, `…/mm/x/yz`.

| query | matches (relative to `…/mm/`) |
|---|---|
| `foo` / `FOO` / `Foo` | `Foo`, `foobar`, `bar/foo` |
| `bar` | `foobar` only (**not** `bar/foo`) |
| `bar foo` | `bar/foo` |
| `foo bar` | `foobar` |
| `mm` | *(none)* |
| `mm/` | `Foo`, `foobar` (**not** `bar/foo`) |
| `mm/foo` | `Foo`, `foobar` |
| `/foo` | `Foo`, `foobar`, `bar/foo` |
| `z`, `yz`, `x/`, `x/y` | `x/yz` |
| `o`, `oo` | `Foo`, `foobar`, `bar/foo` |
| the full absolute path of `Foo` | `Foo`, `foobar` |
| `.` , `..` | *(none — no literal-dot / parent-dir handling)* |

Rule consistent with all observations: keywords are matched **case-insensitively, in order, as substrings** of the full path, and the **end of the last keyword's match must lie after the position of the final `/`** (which is why `bar` and `mm` fail but `mm/` and `x/y` succeed). No `..`/`.`/`-` special handling in `query` (that lives in the shell wrapper). Zero keywords = match everything.

| situation | exit |
|---|---|
